42fdf193.task:
Perform comprehensive reconnaissance and attack-surface mapping of the in-scope web application at http://host.docker.internal:4175 (black-box, no source code available).

GOAL: Produce a complete, actionable endpoint/attack-surface map for downstream vulnerability testing.

TASKS:
1. Initial probe: fetch the root URL with curl/httpx (through the sandbox proxy; do NOT disable it) and capture response headers, status codes, server banner, cookies, and full HTML. Identify the tech stack (framework, language, CMS, frontend framework) from headers/meta/scripts.
2. Crawl the application thoroughly: use katana and/or gospider (bounded: depth ~4-5, keep to the single host, include query params) to enumerate all pages, endpoints, API routes, forms, and parameters. Also use agent-browser with a session named after yourself to click through interactive flows (login, signup, dashboards, etc.) so authenticated/JS-rendered routes are discovered — use `agent-browser --session recon-mapper snapshot -i` after opening pages.
3. JS analysis: collect all JavaScript files, scan for endpoints, API base URLs, hardcoded keys/secrets, and interesting strings.
4. Directory/content discovery: run ffuf with a small-to-medium wordlist (e.g. /usr/share/wordlists/dirb/common.txt or SecLists if present) against the base URL for common paths (/api, /admin, /docs, /swagger, /health, /static, /.git, etc.). Also check for API documentation endpoints (openapi.json, swagger-ui, redoc).
5. Parameter discovery: use arjun on key endpoints to find hidden parameters.
6. Record everything: write a detailed report file at /workspace/recon_report.md (shared location so other agents can read it) with: tech stack, all discovered URLs/endpoints (with methods if known), parameters, cookies/auth scheme, interesting findings (versions, headers, error messages, debug info), and a prioritized list of attack surfaces.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Stay strictly on http://host.docker.internal:4175 (and its own resources). Do not test other hosts.
- Traffic goes through the Caido proxy automatically — that's fine.
- Keep crawls bounded (don't crawl the entire internet or huge wordlists).
- Clean up large raw output files after extracting what you need.
- Do NOT send exploit payloads (no injection/XSS/SQLi testing) — recon only. Just map, fingerprint, and enumerate.
- Note anything interesting (auth pages, file uploads, API endpoints, IDOR-looking params like /resource/<id>, admin panels).

Deliver: a completion report summarizing the attack surface, plus /workspace/recon_report.md with full details.
